title: Evidence for Sequential Υ(nS) Suppression in Light Ion Collisions
hook: Physicists just found the same 'melting pattern' that signals a quark-gluon plasma — the universe's primordial soup — in much smaller particle collisions than ever confirmed before.
key_points: Quarkonia (heavy quark-antiquark pairs) melt at different rates inside a quark-gluon plasma.
Weakly-bound excited states melt faster than tightly-bound ground states — 'sequential suppression.'
CMS measured three bottomonium states in small oxygen-oxygen and neon-neon collisions at the LHC.
The more weakly-bound states were suppressed well below their expected ordinary-collision rates.
The most weakly-bound state's suppression was over 3 standard deviations stronger than the next one's.
This suggests quark-gluon plasma can form in smaller collision systems than previously confirmed.
content_html: A new CMS Collaboration preprint on arXiv uses a clever trick to probe the quark-gluon plasma — the ultra-hot "primordial soup" that briefly filled the universe after the Big Bang and can be recreated in particle collisions. Quarkonia, bound pairs of a heavy quark and its antiquark, melt in that plasma at different rates depending on how tightly bound they are, like differently sized ice cubes melting at different speeds in hot soup: weakly-bound excited states go first, tightly-bound ground states last.
extra_html: The team reported the first measurements of three bottomonium states — Υ(1S), Υ(2S), and Υ(3S) — in the much smaller oxygen-oxygen collisions at the LHC, plus two of them in neon-neon collisions. The more weakly-bound Υ(2S) came out suppressed well below its expected rate from ordinary proton-proton collisions, and the even more weakly-bound Υ(3S) was suppressed further still, by more than 3 standard deviations relative to Υ(2S). That's the same sequential-suppression fingerprint long seen in big lead-lead and gold-gold collisions — now showing up in far smaller, lighter-nucleus collisions, hinting that quark-gluon plasma may form more easily than previously confirmed.

Quark-gluon plasma can only exist in gold-gold and lead-lead collisions
Bottomonium states are unaffected by the quark-gluon plasma
